title: How to export a page in Notion on Mac: PDF, HTML, or Markdown for 2026
metaTitle: How to Export a Page in Notion on Mac (Step by Step)
description: How to export a page in Notion on Mac: the ••• menu path, PDF, HTML, and Markdown options, subpages, and common export errors.

intro: To export a page in Notion on Mac, open the page in the desktop app, click the ••• icon at the top right, choose More, then Export. Pick PDF, HTML, or Markdown & CSV, set the options, and click Export to save the file.
tldr: Open the page, click the ••• icon at the top right, then choose More > Export.
Pick PDF, HTML, or Markdown & CSV. HTML and Markdown exports arrive as a zip file.
Export is not in the Mac menu bar, and Notion documents no keyboard shortcut for it.
The desktop app cannot print directly. Export to PDF, then print the PDF.
For a whole workspace, use Settings > General under Workspace. The link expires after 7 days.

blocks.text: Export one page from the Notion desktop app

Open the page first. Then look at the upper-right corner of the page for the ••• icon. That icon opens the page menu, and export lives inside it, under More. It is not in the Mac menu bar, so skip the menu bar entirely.

Notion's help center describes this same path for single pages. It works from the desktop app and from a page open in a browser. Once the Export window opens, the format you pick decides the rest of the choices.

blocks.title: Labels from Notion's help
blocks.text: Notion's help center gives the ••• > More > Export path. I did not test it on a live Mac, so if a label has moved, look for the same icon and option names.
Choose PDF, HTML, or Markdown & CSV

The format dropdown decides what you get back. PDF gives you one file that looks like the page. HTML and Markdown & CSV give you a zip file instead. Pick the format by what you will do with the file next.

blocks.text: PDF has three settings. Include content lets you export everything, or exclude files and images. Page format sets the paper size. Scale percent is optional, so change it only when the default size looks wrong.

Two PDF limits trip people up. Custom emojis do not appear in PDF exports. Very large exports may also arrive by email instead of starting a download, so check your inbox if nothing downloads after you click Export.
Include subpages: what it does and which plan gets it

Include subpages exports the child pages under the page you chose. For PDF, Notion's help ties this option to Business and Enterprise plans. You get a zip of nested PDFs, and the download link arrives by email.

For HTML and Markdown & CSV, Include subpages is a simple switch. Turn it on before you click Export. With HTML, each page gets its own folder, and its assets are saved separately, so files stay with the page they belong to.

If you do not see the PDF switch, check your plan first. I could not confirm the full plan table on Notion's pricing page, so check it for your plan before you rely on the option. Your admin can also tell you which plan the workspace uses.
Print a Notion page on Mac
The Notion desktop app has no direct print option. Cmd+P does not print either. Notion's keyboard shortcut list shows ⌘ P as search, or as a jump to a recently viewed page.

blocks.title: Cmd+P is not print
blocks.text: ⌘ P opens search in Notion. If you press it expecting a print dialog, you get a search box instead. Export to PDF and print that file.

Here is the route that works. Export the page to PDF using the steps above. Then open the PDF and print it from the app that opens it. Full-page databases cannot be printed this way, so export them to PDF first as well.
In a browser, File > Print works and can save the page as a PDF. That is a second route if the page is already open in a browser tab.
Export from a browser, or open the page in the Mac app

If you work in a browser tab, the export path is the same. Click ••• at the top right of the page, choose More, then Export. If you would rather work in the Mac app, click ••• then More, then Open in Mac app, and the page opens in the desktop app.
Export every page in a workspace at once

Single-page export handles one page at a time. For everything, go to Settings > General under Workspace, then select Export all workspace content. Notion emails you a download link. That link expires after 7 days, so download the file the same week.

A whole-workspace export works on desktop or web only. It can take up to 30 hours, depending on how big the workspace is. Private pages of other users are left out, and teamspace settings can exclude more content.

Be careful with PDF at workspace level. Notion's backup help says that option is going away, with an August 31, 2026 deadline. That date has passed. I could not confirm full removal, so check the export dialog before you plan around it.

Individual pages can still be exported as PDF. Workspace exports remain available as HTML, Markdown, or CSV. A workspace export also cannot be reimported to rebuild the workspace, according to Notion's backup help, so treat it as an archive.
Fix export errors and failed downloads

Most export problems come from four causes. The link expired, the workspace is too large, the Export option is missing, or the page is not visible to you. Each cause has a specific fix in Notion's help center.
If a PDF export fails, Notion exports HTML instead. So check what file arrived before you assume you have a PDF. If a whole workspace export fails, Notion's backup help suggests a batch workaround.

Use the batch workaround when the workspace is too big. Open a top-level page, click •••, choose Export, pick a format, and turn on Include subpages. Repeat for each top-level page you need, rather than running one giant export.
No Export option in the ••• menu? A workspace or teamspace may have disabled it. Guests need Full access to export. Ask an admin before you spend time hunting for the option.
Mistakes people make when exporting from Notion on Mac
The first mistake is looking for Export in the menu bar. It lives under the ••• icon on the page. The second is pressing ⌘ P and expecting a printer. It opens search instead.
The third mistake is forgetting Include subpages on a parent page. You then get one page when you wanted the whole section. Check the switch before you click Export, every time.

The fourth is opening an HTML or Markdown export without unzipping it. Double click the zip first, then open the folder for the page you need. The fifth is sharing a zip with a Windows user who cannot extract it. Paths over 260 characters block extraction on Windows. Ask them to use 7-Zip, or re-export with Create folders for subpages unchecked. I could not confirm that checkbox appears in the Mac dialog.
Check your macOS and Notion version before you export
The Notion desktop app needs macOS 13 or later. Notion's system requirements page gives that as the minimum. If your Mac runs an older version, use Notion in a browser for export.

Notion's help does not list a build number for the Mac app. To check for updates, open the Notion menu and choose Check for Updates. Notion says the app updates itself, and ⌘ R refreshes it to show new features.

You may see version 7.42.3 in a third-party listing. Homebrew's Notion cask shows that number and also needs macOS 13 or later. The number comes from Homebrew, not from Notion, so treat it as a hint only.
Ask Lazur where the export controls are

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ (Option and Command) and ask about anything on your screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a control is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.

Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. With a page open, you can ask 'where is the export button' or 'walk me through exporting as PDF'. Lazur points at the ••• icon, then waits while you click.
Lazur does not click for you, and it does not run the export. It is not a plugin for Notion, and it does not change your pages. You stay in control of every click.
Next steps after you export

Open the file to check it. For a PDF, scroll through the layout, the images, and the paper size. For HTML or Markdown, unzip the file and open the folder for the page. A quick check now saves a second export later.
If you only need someone to read the page, a share link may suit better. The guide covers permissions and links in [how to share a page in Notion on Mac](/how-to/share-a-page-in-notion).
If the page sits on your iPhone, the share menu includes AirDrop. You can send a PDF from there to your Mac. That route skips the desktop app entirely.

Not set up yet? The [install guide for the Notion desktop app](/how-to/install-the-desktop-app-in-notion) covers macOS 13 and later. When you want a voice guide for your screen, the [Lazur download](/download) is the next step.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to export a page in Notion on Mac?
faq.answer: Not one that Notion documents. Its keyboard shortcut help lists no shortcut for exporting or printing a page. Some third-party cheat sheets disagree with each other, so use the ••• menu path instead.

faq.question: Where is Export on a Mac?
faq.answer: Export is not in the Mac menu bar. Open the page, click the ••• icon in the upper-right corner, choose More, then Export.

faq.question: Can I print a Notion page on Mac?
faq.answer: The desktop app has no direct print option. Export the page to PDF, then print the PDF. In a browser, File > Print works and can save the page as a PDF.

faq.question: Which format should I pick: PDF, HTML, or Markdown & CSV?
faq.answer: Pick PDF for a fixed copy to read or print. Pick HTML for a browsable offline copy. Pick Markdown & CSV when you need the text in another tool, since full-page databases become CSV.

faq.question: Does exporting a page include its subpages?
faq.answer: Only if you turn on Include subpages. For PDF, Notion's help ties that option to Business and Enterprise plans. For HTML and Markdown & CSV, it is a switch you can turn on before you click Export.

faq.question: How do I export my whole Notion workspace on Mac?
faq.answer: Go to Settings > General under Workspace, then select Export all workspace content. You get an emailed link that expires after 7 days, and the export can take up to 30 hours.

faq.question: Why did my export arrive by email?
faq.answer: Very large exports may arrive by email rather than starting a download. Check your inbox, and your spam folder, for the link to the file.

faq.question: Will custom emojis show up in a PDF export?
faq.answer: No. Notion's export help says custom emojis do not appear in PDF exports. Check the file before you send it to anyone.

faq.question: Can Lazur export the page for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at the ••• icon and guides you one click at a time. It does not click buttons or run the export for you.

steps.name: Open the page in the Notion desktop app
steps.text: Open Notion and go to the page you want to export. If the page is open in a browser, click ••• then More, then Open in Mac app to open it in the desktop app first.
steps.tip: Notion says the desktop app updates automatically, so you rarely need to reinstall it.

steps.name: Click the ••• icon on the page
steps.text: Look at the upper-right corner of the page. Click the ••• icon to open the page menu. It sits inside the page, not in the Mac menu bar.

steps.name: Open More, then choose Export
steps.text: In the page menu, open More. Then choose Export. The Export window opens with the format options.

steps.name: Pick PDF, HTML, or Markdown & CSV
steps.text: Open the format dropdown in the Export window and select PDF, HTML, or Markdown & CSV. Pick the format based on what you will do with the file next.

steps.name: Set the PDF options if you chose PDF
steps.text: Open Include content and choose everything, or exclude files and images. Set Page format for paper size. Change Scale percent only if the default does not fit your page.
steps.tip: Custom emojis do not appear in PDF exports, so plan around that before you share the file.

steps.name: Switch on Include subpages if you need child pages
steps.text: Turn on Include subpages when the page has child pages you want. For PDF, this option is limited to Business and Enterprise plans, and the download link arrives by email. For HTML and Markdown & CSV, it is a simple switch.
steps.tip: If you do not see the PDF switch, check your plan before you assume the option is gone.

steps.name: Click Export and wait for the file
steps.text: Click Export. A download usually starts. Very large exports may arrive by email instead, so check your inbox if nothing downloads.
steps.tip: If a PDF export fails, Notion exports HTML instead. Check the file type before you share it.

steps.name: Unzip HTML and Markdown exports
steps.text: HTML and Markdown & CSV exports arrive as a zip file. Double click the zip to extract it, then open the folder for the page you need.
steps.tip: Long file paths can block extraction on Windows. Use 7-Zip there if the zip will not open.

troubleshooting.problem: No Export option in the ••• menu
troubleshooting.fix: A workspace or teamspace admin may have turned export off. Guests need Full access. Ask an admin before you keep looking.
Run the export again to get a new link. Whole-workspace links expire after 7 days.

troubleshooting.problem: A PDF export failed and an HTML file arrived
troubleshooting.fix: Notion exports HTML when a PDF fails. Open the HTML file in a browser, or export the PDF again later.
Export top-level pages one at a time with Include subpages turned on, as Notion's backup help suggests.
Paths over 260 characters can block extraction. Export with Create folders for subpages unchecked, or extract the zip with 7-Zip.

troubleshooting.problem: A page is missing from the workspace export
troubleshooting.fix: Private pages of other users are excluded. Teamspace settings can also exclude some content.
